text:
alex: hey @support — customer reports invoice > local SDK estimates for a small batch of completion calls. they say local estimator shows ~120 tokens per call but invoice shows ~138.

soumya: thanks alex. any repro payloads? are these streaming calls or single-shot completions?

alex: single-shot completion via our python sdk. sending cURL too. customer says no function calls in prompt.

megan: can you paste the exact request (headers + body) they used? also any proxy / sidecar?

alex: here is the curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-2-13b","input":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":150}'
```

alex: and the python snippet they used locally (sdk estimator):
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="sk-...")
est = c.estimate_tokens(prompt="Summarize: ...", model="rwd-llama-2-13b")
print(est)
```

ryan: quick check: is the customer using our hosted "private prefill" or any route rule that injects system context? that would add tokens invisibly.

alex: they say no custom prefill. But they are on dedicated, and we do have an autocomplete policy that adds a small system note for analytics.

marcus: billing-bot pulled the invoice lines for the first 3 requests (trace ids stripped). looks like each of those had +18 prefill tokens on the server side. i can paste sanitized snippet.

billing-bot: invoice lines (sanitized):
- request_id=rx-01 token_count=138 model=rwd-llama-2-13b
- request_id=rx-02 token_count=140 model=rwd-llama-2-13b
- request_id=rx-03 token_count=137 model=rwd-llama-2-13b

alex: ok that's consistent with customer's numbers. where are those +18 tokens coming from? sdk estimator didn't see them.

soumya: possible sources: server-side system instruction, injected tool preamble, or function call metadata (even if function not invoked). check server logs for "Injected-Preamble" or header X-Redwood-Injected.

megan: also confirm if the client used streaming termination or stop tokens; our estimator might omit trailing stop/pad tokens depending on API parity.

alex: searching logs now... found lines: `Injected-Preamble: {"type":"analytics","text":"session_id:abc123"}` (not in customer curl). that preamble is added by the gateway for Dedicated customers for routing metrics.

ryan: ah — gateway prefill is not included in SDK estimator by design. estimator approximates only user-supplied prompt + completion. server-side prefill/preamble and invisible tool metadata are billed though.

alex: customer surprised. they built internal billing match to sdk.

megan: proposal: for Dedicated we should (1) document prefill behavior clearly, (2) expose header X-Redwood-Prefill-Tokens on response so clients can reconcile, and (3) add an option for tenants to opt-out of analytics prefill.

soumya: immediate remediation: tell customer to check the response header we already emit for some routes: `X-Redwood-Prefill-Count`. if they're not seeing it, gateway version may be old.

alex: customer checked, header absent. they are on an older Dedicated gateway build.

marcus: ops note: we will roll a patch to include X-Redwood-Prefill-Count for all Dedicated gateways in next 24h.

alex: for support answer to customer: explain that invisible gateway prefill adds N tokens (we see ~18), provide them the invoice lines, and offer to help patch the estimator script to add that static offset as a short-term fix.

megan: also add this as a KB: "Why SDK estimates can be lower than invoice" — include cases: server prefill, tool-call preambles, streaming sentinel tokens, and hidden function meta. give repro steps and how to surface X-Redwood-Prefill-Count.

soumya: followup: can someone collect a minimal reproducible test (curl + gateway logs) and attach to this thread so I can file an RFC to change estimator behavior?

alex: i'll coordinate with the customer to get a trace id. meanwhile i've advised them to expect discrepancy; sending the sanitized invoice rows and suggested short-term estimator patch. :thumbsup:

megan: thanks. tagging @ryan to schedule the gateway opt-out feature in Dedicated roadmap.

ryan: got it. logging roadmap issue. thanks all.
